$comment: PRE-REGISTERED adoption gate for is_circumstantial v2. Committed BEFORE any blind label exists and before the classifier's author has seen a single rating. Same rule as pass_bars.json and v3_expected_shape.json: a criterion written after seeing the agreement figure is not a criterion. Changing anything here is its own explicit commit that says why.
what_is_being_decided: whether the state_coverage denominator moves from is_circumstantial v1 (first person + factual marker) to v2 (first person + a term the persona's P/B/J facts carry that no offered graph fact does).

adoption_criterion.rule: v2 is adopted IFF it agrees with the blind labels BETTER than v1 does, over the same 53 segments.
adoption_criterion.why_comparative: an absolute figure is uninterpretable. 'v2 agrees 85%' means nothing without knowing whether v1 agrees 70% or 90%, and the question on the table is not whether v2 is good but whether it is better than what ships today.
report: simple agreement for v1 and for v2
Cohen's kappa for v1 and for v2, because the classes are unbalanced and raw agreement flatters a classifier that mostly says the majority class
every disagreement, BOTH directions, enumerated with its segment text
adoption_criterion.read_the_disagreements: a v2 miss that is a principled edge case is a different object from one that is a hole in the definition. The enumeration is not decoration; it is how that distinction gets made.
adoption_criterion.clustering_clause: if v2 beats v1 but its misses CLUSTER in one identifiable class, that class is recorded as a NAMED LIMITATION of instrument v2 — never as a silent tolerance, and never fixed by editing the classifier until it stops missing them, which would be fitting to the labels.

metric_split.rule: instrument v2 reports TWO numbers, never one.
metric_split.state_coverage: over circumstantial segments that a P/B/J id COULD cover.
metric_split.schema_gap_rate: share of circumstantial segments that no id in the declared surface can cover.
metric_split.derivation: from principle, not from the eight segments that raised it: a coverage metric computed over segments nothing in the schema can express measures the SCHEMA, not the model. Blending the two produces a number that falls when the model gets worse and also when the surface gets narrower, and cannot say which happened.
metric_split.known_uncoverable_class: symptoms. PROFILE_FIELDS does not carry them and biomarkers are deliberately outside it, so 'I feel breathless most days' asserts a circumstance with no available id. That is a coverage finding to log, exactly as the module docstring already says for an unsimulated persona's missing event log.
metric_split.who_adjudicates: the labels. The rater labels the CONCEPT — does this segment assert a fact about the speaker's own circumstances, and could the declared surface support it — and the classifier's job is to approximate that, never to define it.

floors_are_instrument_relative.rule: a coverage floor is stamped with the instrument version it was registered against, and does not transfer across an instrument change.

v3_floor.status: unchanged, and v0.4 remains adjudicated under it

floors_are_instrument_relative.consequence: v2 reading 0.6000 on the v3 cassette is NOT a pass against the v3 floor. It is a number from a different denominator that happens to land on the old bar, which is the most suspicious shape a rewritten metric can take and is reported as a coincidence rather than a result.
floors_are_instrument_relative.before_v4: adopting v2 re-registers the floor against the label-validated denominator, in its own commit, BEFORE any v4 run exists. A bar that silently survives an instrument change is a bar that means nothing.

conflicts_of_interest.consequence: the author cannot rate. Labels come from an independent rater working from segment text alone — no personas, no citations, no kinds, no classifier verdicts — so the validation cannot inherit the classifier's token-match logic.
conflicts_of_interest.sheet: 53 segments, hash-shuffled so the classes are not grouped.
